Maya — attached a first-pass workbook. I built two scenarios: Scenario A assumes a retroactive milestone rebate (paid as a credit memo to reseller, applied to future invoices); Scenario B assumes an up-front rebate passed through immediately as a reduced list price.

Notes included in the workbook: how we allocate seller-fee (marketplace fee) and where reseller commission is recorded. In our standard flows reseller uplift is handled as a credit memo when it's retroactive; immediate pass-throughs are reflected by adjusting list price on the private offer.

High-level impacts:
- Retroactive rebate (credit memo): Redwood books gross at list, then records a contra revenue/credit at quarter close — shows as a reduction in net revenue and triggers a revenue deferral in some cases.
- Immediate pass-through: reduces billed list price and is cleaner for procurement but can reduce our reported ARPU.

Attachment: reseller_margin_workbook.xlsx (Excel)
